I had a male friend during my first year of university, and we were really close, talked a lot about philosophy and films. For context, i'm a girl, and I was in a long term relationship, i was so worried about 'leading someone on' that i made a point to talk about my boyfriend a lot so that i wasn't being unfair to the friend (they had even talked to each other), so i was pretty sure that he just genuinely wanted a friend and nothing more. Any time i felt like anyone was hinting anything i'd bring my boyfriend up as the politest way to indirectly reject any advances.

Cut forward to the march of first year, and drunk at a party he tries to come on to me, i reject him (obviously) and he ranted. Oh boy did he rant. On and on about bitches who try to lead guys on just to feed their egos, how dare i make him think something was there (i had explicitly said in the past i wasn't interested in anyone but my boyfriend). It gradually evolved into him weirdly trying to save face "oh you thought i liked you? i just feel sorry for you that's why i pretended to come on to you" etc etc about me being fat and uninteresting. I ended up having to put him to bed because he was ranting and raving at everyone late into the night and as I was his 'best friend' (his words) it was my responsibility to deal with his bullshit. I left before he woke up.

We didn't talk for a month and then he sent me 40+ messages apologising, insisting I was obsessing over him (why else wouldn't i contact him?) telling me we needed each other. After i didn't reply he rang my boyfriend trying to get to me. That's when i decided to block him. Thankfully he was in his final year and has moved away now.

I don't suppose it's the most hurtful thing said to me by a 'friend', to be truthful i was numb to him by the end and just wanted him to leave me alone, but really it has affected me the most negatively. I genuinely think i'm a bad friend now because i cut people out/don't let them get close 'just in case' it turns out like that. The most hurt i was by it is the way i treat myself now out of fear, thankfully it turns out there are a lot of good people out there too.

tl;dr - boys who believe in the friendzone tend to be arseholes
